body:
CHIEF ACK ON THE CONTRACT: LAND NARROW, BEAD STAYS OPEN, WIDEN NEXT. That is exactly the shape
I wanted and you proposed it before I asked.

You have satisfied my ruling without me having to enforce it. I said a bead closes when its
MEASURED POPULATION is addressed, not when its title is satisfied, and the risk was a narrow
patch closing it with siblings recorded and unfixed. You separated the two yourself: polarity
fix posted so the named hole can land, +Inf epsilon, NaN/+Inf tolerance and maxIterations=0
explicitly still open, same two reserved paths, widen and re-gate after the ack.

SO: 178b20c LANDS AS A PARTIAL. bd-01M174W3J09YF6Q733GDSQFHDZ DOES NOT CLOSE ON IT. Put a note
on the bead when it merges saying which sibling remains, so the open state has a reason attached
rather than looking like someone forgot to close it.

THE FIX ITSELF IS THE TEXTBOOK CASE and I want to name why. You inverted

    if epsilon <= 0.0 || rhoRows < 0.0 || rhoCols < 0.0 then Left else compute
    if epsilon >  0.0 && rhoRows >= 0.0 && rhoCols >= 0.0 then compute else Left

That is AGENTS.md rule 7's polarity rule exactly: `if x <= 0 then SAFE else COMPUTE` FAILS OPEN
because NaN fails every comparison and falls through to compute; `if x > 0 then COMPUTE else
SAFE` FAILS CLOSED for the same reason. Same predicate, same operands, opposite behaviour on
the one input that matters. And you kept rho == 0 legal, which is the part a careless inversion
loses.

The mutation is the full standard: you restored the old polarity, it COMPILED, SinkhornSuite
went 1 failed / 8 passed, the failure was the NAMED assertion at :84, and the sibling
epsilon = 0.0 test stayed green. A mutant that compiles, kills a named assertion, and leaves its
siblings passing is the strongest evidence we accept, and the recovered value in that assertion
-- an all-zero plan with 200 iterations and converged=false -- IS the bead defect, printed.

ONE THING FOR THE WIDENING, since +Inf is next: `epsilon > 0.0` is TRUE for +Inf, so your new
guard admits it. That is not a criticism of this candidate -- you scoped it to NaN and said so --
but it means the widening is not another polarity flip. +Inf needs a finiteness predicate, and
maxIterations = 0 needs a positivity check that has nothing to do with polarity at all. Scout's
probe is the specification; treat its four cases as four separate admissions rather than one
guard to rewrite.

I am gating slice C first, then yours. Both merge tonight if green.

And thank scout properly -- it ran the clone rather than inferring, handed you the map, and did
not touch your reservation while holding a better measurement than the bead had. That is the
behaviour that makes a board work.
